Survey of prior English translations of Trithemius

The survey located no prior complete published English translation for 23 of the 29 texts. Those 23 texts account for 41 catalogue records drawn from 39 digitized sources. The full translated catalogue has 47 records and 45 sources. This is a search outcome, not proof of translation priority. This document records what was checked, what was found, and where the uncertainty lies. It is a working bibliography, not an exhaustive one; corrections via the issue tracker are welcome.

Method and limits

Checked: standard reference works on Trithemius (Klaus Arnold, Johannes Trithemius 1462–1516), the WorldCat/KVK union catalogues, the esotericarchives.com and trithemius.com bibliographies, and targeted searches for each work's Latin title plus "English translation". This is a secondary-literature survey, not an archival one — an unpublished thesis translation or a journal appendix could exist for any "first in English" work below without surfacing. Treat "no published English translation found" as not located, not as proven never translated.

Works with a prior published English translation

Prefer these editions for scholarly citation; the renderings in this corpus are independent machine-assisted translations included for coverage.

Work (corpus id) Prior English
De Laude Scriptorum Manualium (prdl-24362) Roland Behrendt, In Praise of Scribes, ed. Klaus Arnold (Coronado Press, 1974); Elizabeth Bongie (Alcuin Society, 1977)
De Septem Secundeis (prdl-24383) William Lilly's 1647 The World's Catastrophe is an early English version/adaptation; modern occult-press reissues exist
Steganographia tradition — clavis works (prdl-70281, prdl-70282) The Steganographia itself: a partial English (Books I–II) has circulated since the early 1980s; the comprehensive scholarly edition is Stephen Skinner & Daniel Clark, Steganographia: Books I–IV (Llewellyn, 2024). These corpus works are the clavis (key) texts and adjacent cipher-mechanics prose, from different source editions.
Polygraphia (prdl-24389, prdl-24390, prdl-24391) Only Philip Neal's partial translation of the prefatory matter. Gabriel de Collange's French Polygraphie (1561) is the long-standing vernacular witness. The continuous English of the body in this corpus is, as far as could be determined, a first.

Works with no prior complete published English translation located

The following works are among those for which the survey located no complete published English translation. For the Eight Questions, the survey records English excerpts.

  • Monastic reform: De Statu et Ruina Monastici Ordinis, De Triplici Regione Claustralium (3 eds.), De Republica Ecclesiae et Monachorum Ordinis (2 records of the same scan), Sermones et Exhortationes ad Monachos (2), Abbreviatura Recessuum Capitularium, the Admonitiones ad Monachos collection
  • Priestly/pastoral: De Cura Pastorali, Institutio Vitae Sacerdotalis (2), De Sacerdotum Vita Instituenda
  • Marian/hagiographic: De Laudibus Sanctissimae Matris Annae (6 records from 5 sources), De Purissima et Immaculata Conceptione Virginis (2), De Laudibus Ordinis Fratrum Carmelitarum
  • Devotional: De Operatione Divini Amoris, De Vanitate et Miseria Humanae Vitae, De Vera Conversione Mentis ad Deum
  • Bibliographic/historical: Liber de Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis (2 eds.), the Opera Historica / Chronicon Hirsaugiense and Chronicon Sponheimense, the Compendium sive Breviarium of Frankish origins
  • Liber Octo Quaestionum (4 eds.) — only excerpts have appeared in English
  • Veterum Sophorum Sigilla et Imagines Magicae (2) — an attributed text of uncertain authenticity; no scholarly English located

The corpus retains Hucbald’s Ecloga de laude calvorum (prdl-24376) as part of the printed collection. Its survey coverage remains incomplete. Coverage of the two individual Clavis texts and the completeness of Lilly’s adaptation of De Septem Secundeis also remain unresolved. The catalogue counts these four witnesses separately.

For De Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis in particular: it has been heavily used by historians of bibliography in the Latin for centuries, but no complete published English edition was located.

A note on overlap and credit

Acknowledging a prior translation is scholarly courtesy, not an admission of derivation: every rendering in this corpus is produced independently by the pipeline described in ../METHODOLOGY.md from digitizations of public-domain Latin texts. Where a prior English edition exists, the intro headnote for that work names it and recommends it for citation. The retrieval anchors used by the pipeline are public-domain only (see ../data/anchors/CURATION.md and METHODOLOGY.md §5); no in-copyright translation was used as a source or an anchor.

Classification used by the catalogue

Of the 47 translated catalogue records, two have complete prior English translations and four have unresolved survey coverage. The catalogue’s “no prior complete English located” filter covers the other 41 records from 39 sources, representing 23 distinct texts. These include three Polygraphia witnesses with translated prefatory matter, four Eight Questions witnesses with translated excerpts, and 34 records from 32 sources for which the survey located no prior published English.
